title: 10 Identity Resolution Use Cases for Marketers
summary: Explore 10 identity resolution use cases that help marketers unify customer data, personalize campaigns, improve targeting, and measure marketing performance.
body_markdown:
Identity resolution is the key to unlocking a unified view of the customer, which too often gets lost across disconnected digital and offline touchpoints. Without it, you risk duplicated ad spend, poorly timed messages, and disjointed customer experiences.[Identity resolution](https://liveramp.com/blog/what-is-identity-resolution/) solves these issues by unifying signals into a single, persistent profile that preserves privacy.


From activation to analytics, identity resolution use cases span every stage of the customer lifecycle, and they’re fast becoming table stakes for any data-driven[identity strategy](https://liveramp.com/blog/why-a-trustworthy-identity-strategy-is-essential-for-marketers/) .


Let’s take a closer look at 10 ways you can use identity resolution to unify data, strengthen customer connections, and ultimately drive measurable marketing outcomes.


## Key takeaways


- Identity resolution unifies fragmented online and offline customer data into a single, accurate profile for each individual.
- Use cases fall into five strategic categories – resolve, build, enrich, protect, and connect – that each play a role in improving targeting, personalization, and measurement.
- Practical applications for identity resolution span the full customer lifecycle, from cleaning and consolidating records to powering advanced attribution for marketing campaigns.
- [Identity resolution platforms](https://liveramp.com/our-platform/identity-resolution-translation) preserve data protections while still enabling activation, enrichment, and collaboration at scale.


## Five strategic categories behind identity resolution use cases


Identity resolution use cases draw on five categories – resolve, build, enrich, protect, and connect - that help you turn fragmented customer data into actionable insights and more relevant experiences


### Resolve fragmented customer identities


Resolving disparate and fragmented customer records enables you to establish a single, accurate view of each individual customer. In the process, you eliminate duplicate profiles and connect online identifiers with offline data, ensuring a clean, consistent identity foundation that drives reliable targeting, personalization, and measurement.


### Build a shared identity foundation


Once you’ve resolved customer identities across platforms, it’s time to build on that foundation by creating an enterprise-wide identity framework that connects data across every channel, team, and platform. Building this infrastructure creates a shared foundation that supports long-term agility and consistent customer insights across the organization.


### Enrich customer profiles with additional data


After resolving identities, brands often find that they still have gaps in their first-party data. LiveRamp’s[Contact and Attribute Enrichment](https://liveramp.com/our-platform/enrichment) solutions help fill those gaps by enriching existing customer records with missing demographic and behavioral attributes. This enables more precise segmentation and better activation across channels.


### **Protect customer data through governance controls**


Identity resolution platforms are built to help data be activated and shared responsibly without exposing sensitive information. As privacy regulations tighten and security concerns grow, these features support the safeguards needed to collaborate with partners and run campaigns while keeping consumer data secure. **‍**


### **Connect with customers across channels**


Above all, identity resolution enables you to build stronger, more authentic connections with your customers. Once identities are resolved, built, and enriched with data governance protections in place, you can activate data for omnichannel engagement at scale while ensuring attribution measurement is accurate.


The following use cases show how these categories support your marketing goals.


## 10 practical applications of identity resolution


### 1. Build a unified customer profile across all touchpoints


Building a unified customer profile is a foundational element of any identity strategy. All other identity resolution use cases depend on it.


Identity resolution tools connect fragmented identifiers like emails, phone numbers, cookies, device IDs, and offline transaction data, creating a single view of each customer. From there, the platform assigns each individual a unique, person-based ID that maintains consistency across systems while supporting privacy program requirements.


This complete profile not only improves customer understanding but but helps activation and measurement efforts draw on more consistent customer data.


The world’s leading job site[Indeed](https://liveramp.com/customer-stories/indeed/) used LiveRamp’s[AWS Embedded Identity Resolution](https://liveramp.com/blog/embedded-identity-solutions) to unify fragmented data directly in the cloud, without the need to move sensitive records. Consolidating its first-party data ultimately resulted in a 54% increase in Indeed’s re-targeting audience size and a 20% boost in ad response rates, demonstrating the measurable impact of a strong identity foundation.


### 2. Connect offline purchase data to digital channels


For many brands, some of the most valuable insights live in offline purchase data, but those signals often sit disconnected from digital campaigns. Identity resolution closes this gap by tying in-store transactions to persistent customer IDs, which can then be matched against online identifiers like emails, cookies, or device IDs.


This process happens through a secure[data onboarding](https://liveramp.com/blog/a-primer-on-data-onboarding) workflow: first-party transaction data is pseudonymized, resolved to an enterprise identity spine, and then translated into digital identifiers that can be used for[data activation](https://liveramp.com/blog/what-is-data-activation-and-how-does-it-work) across platforms. With this bridge in place, marketers can see how real-world purchases influence digital behavior and vice versa.


### 3. Reduce duplicate customer records


Duplicate records are one of the most common data quality problems marketers face. A single customer might appear multiple times across systems under slightly different identifiers: for example, one record tied to an email address and another to a loyalty ID with a second email address. Left unresolved, these duplicates inflate audience counts and lead to wasted ad spend as the same individual is targeted multiple times.


Identity resolution platforms use[deterministic and probabilistic](https://liveramp.com/uk/blog/probabilistic-vs-deterministic-matching) signals to recognize when multiple records belong to the same person and unify them into a single ID. This clean identity spine ensures reporting reflects true reach and frequency and improves segmentation accuracy for more efficient media spend.


### 4. Create behavior-based audience segments


While[audience segmentation](https://liveramp.com/blog/audience-segmentation-with-ai-how-it-works-and-why-it-matters) based on demographic information like location or age becomes more accurate with identity resolution, adding behavioral data into the mix makes targeting even more sophisticated.


With a robust,[enterprise-wide identity framework](https://liveramp.com/solutions/enterprise-identity) in place, you can create behavior-based audience segments by combining transactional, engagement, and loyalty data into richer, more accurate profiles. For example, a sports apparel brand might use purchase, browsing, and loyalty data to segment customers by product interest – such as footwear vs. athletic wear – for more relevant ad targeting.


### **5. Expand audience reach through partner and data marketplace interoperability**


Connecting customer profiles with trusted partner data and[data marketplaces](https://liveramp.com/our-platform/data-marketplace) helps marketers expand audience reach and improve targeting precision.


LiveRamp gives brands a unique advantage by supporting native integration with third-party reference graphs, unlike many competitors that operate in closed ecosystems.


It allows you to scale campaigns by matching with more customers across more channels and discover new high-value audiences while still maintaining control.


{{maximizing-third-party-data-strategy}}


### 6. Identify at-risk customers and support retention


It’s difficult to spot warning signs for customer churn when you lack full visibility into customer behavior and purchase patterns. Identity resolution connects purchase, engagement, and loyalty data to the same customer profile, giving analytics tools a more complete foundation for identifying potential churn signals. You can use these insights to identify which customers are most at risk and proactively trigger retention actions, such as personalized offers or timely outreach.


### 7. Enable secure, responsible data collaboration with partners


As third-party cookies fade across the web, marketers are increasingly turning to[data collaboration](https://liveramp.com/data-collaboration-explainer/) to fill audience gaps. Identity resolution makes this possible by enabling responsible collaboration for joint analytics, measurement, and campaign activation.


Using person-based identifiers created during the identity resolution process, brands can match IDs with partners inside a neutral environment such as a[clean room](https://liveramp.com/data-clean-rooms/) , which helps build trust and prevent data misuse by providing a secure environment for collaboration while ensuring each party’s privacy and governance controls are enforced.


What might data collaboration look like? Biopharmaceutical leader[AbbVie](https://liveramp.com/customer-stories/abbvie/) provides a strong example.


By using the LiveRamp Clean Room, the company was able to connect impression, website, and conversion data in real time without moving or sharing sensitive information. With real-time visibility into how customers respond to messages, the brand can deliver more tailored content that drives stronger engagement.


### 8: Translate identities in secure data clean rooms


When multiple partners bring their own identifiers to the table, aligning them can be a challenge. Identity resolution solves this by translating different partner IDs into a common identity spine within a secure clean room. This makes it possible to conduct joint analysis, measurement, and campaign activation without ever moving or exposing raw data.


LiveRamp’s full interoperability provides a key advantage here. Unlike[cloud-native clean room solutions](https://liveramp.com/blog/liveramp-clean-room-architecture) that lack a native offline graph, LiveRamp can seamlessly connect online and offline identifiers, ensuring more accurate matches and greater scale.


#### 9. Activate personalized marketing campaigns across channels and devices


Activation is the stage where unified identity turns into customer engagement. With persistent profiles in place, marketers can push audiences into ad platforms,[DSPs](https://liveramp.com/uk/blog/what-is-dsp-demand-side-platform-definition) , email service providers, or retail media networks to deliver campaigns that reach the right people, in the right place, at the right time.


Persistent identifiers also make it possible to sequence messages across channels and suppress audiences who have already converted to ensure every interaction feels relevant while eliminating wasted spend.


#### 10. Improve attribution and performance measurement accuracy


Accurate[cross-channel attribution](https://liveramp.com/uk/blog/how-cross-channel-attribution-works) has always been a challenge. When customer journeys span multiple platforms, it’s nearly impossible to see which touchpoints are actually driving results.


But because identity resolution tools tie each customer interaction to a persistent ID, you can gain clarity on how different channels work together to drive conversions, rather than relying on siloed or last-touch attribution reporting. As a result, you can strategically allocate your budget to the channels and tactics that truly influence outcomes.

## ‍ **Identity resolution FAQs**


### What is enterprise identity?


Enterprise identity is a framework that unifies online and offline customer data from every channel, platform, and source into a unified profile that’s assigned a unique identifier. It’s essential for eliminating data silos, gaining a clear view of your customer, and optimizing marketing outcomes.


### How is enterprise identity different from traditional identity resolution?


Traditional identity resolution often works within limited ecosystems or channels, while enterprise identity spans the entire organization. It connects data across business units, partners, and platforms, ensuring interoperability and long-term scalability.


### What types of data can identity resolution connect?


Identity resolution can resolve a wide range of identifiers like emails, phone numbers, cookies, device IDs, loyalty IDs, and transaction data into a unified customer profile. It can also associate purchase records and engagement data with that profile, supporting use cases such as audience segmentation, personalized marketing, and campaign measurement. This flexibility ensures all signals contribute to a more complete customer view.


### How does identity resolution protect customer privacy?


Identity resolution can support customer privacy through safeguards such as pseudonymization, encryption, and privacy-enhancing technologies like clean rooms to ensure that[PII](https://liveramp.com/uk/blog/what-is-personally-identifiable-information-pii) is strictly controlled. It enables secure data sharing and collaboration without compromising compliance.


### **How does identity resolution handle multiple email addresses for the same person?**


Identity resolution tools can connect different email addresses using other shared identifiers, such as a customer ID, verified phone number, or authenticated account activity. Depending on the platform, matching rules and reference data help determine whether records belong to the same individual.


### **How can marketers measure the success of an identity resolution use case?**


Success measures should reflect the selected application. Examples include fewer duplicate customer profiles, more customers matched to activation channels, or more transactions connected to campaign exposure. Establish a baseline before implementation, then assess data quality improvements alongside relevant marketing outcomes.
